prompt:
You are commissioning the speed drive of a permanent-magnet DC motor on a test bench. The bench is simulated; treat it as a real one.

Drive
- A bridge fed from a 48 V supply makes the armature voltage, -48..48 V.
- Current loop: PI at 10 kHz, voltage = Kp_i * e + Ki_i * integral of e dt, e = current reference - measured current (A), output limited to the supply, with anti-windup. The voltage it computes is applied one sample (0.1 ms) later. The current sensor has some noise.
- Speed loop: PI at 1 kHz, current reference = Kp_w * e + Ki_w * integral of e dt, e = speed reference - measured speed (rpm), limited to +/-7.2 A, the drive's rated current. Optional anti-windup (integration stops while the output is limited). Optional first-order filter on the measured speed (time constant in ms).
- Speed is measured with a 1024-line encoder (4096 counts per revolution), as the count difference over each 1 ms speed loop sample.
- Overcurrent trip: if the motor current ever exceeds 10.8 A (1.5 times the rated current), the bridge switches off. set_mode starts it again.
- A dynamometer on the shaft can apply a braking torque, and can lock the shaft at standstill.
- Resistance, inductance, torque constant and inertia are not given. Find out what you need by experimenting.

Modes: "off"; "voltage" (you set the armature voltage directly, no current control); "current" (you set the current reference, speed loop off); "speed" (cascade: you set the speed reference in rpm). Now the motor is at rest, the drive off. Factory gains: current Kp 0.5 V/A, Ki 50 V/(A s); speed Kp 0.002 A/rpm, Ki 0.02 A/(rpm s), no anti-windup, no speed filter.

Acceptance test. It runs after you call submit, with the gains you leave:
1. From rest in speed mode, at t = 20 ms the speed reference steps from 0 to 3380 rpm.
2. 1100 ms later the dynamometer applies 0.293 Nm; 130 ms after that it releases it; the test ends 130 ms later.
Requirements, on the true speed:
- no overcurrent trip;
- within +/-1 % of 3380 rpm no later than 375 ms after the reference step, and staying there until the load;
- overshoot at most 1 %;
- speed error at most 26 rpm when the load goes on and when it comes off;
- back within +/-1 % within 5 ms after each, and staying there.

You have 30 s of motor time and at most 40 tool calls. Work like a drives engineer: identify the motor, tune the current loop, then the speed loop, check on the bench, then call submit.

steps.text: First the electrical data with the shaft locked: a small voltage step, a few percent of the supply, so the locked-rotor current stays far below the trip. Resistance from the final current, inductance from the 63 % rise time.

steps.name: run
steps.summary: ran to 30.0 ms in voltage mode: speed 0 -> 0 rpm, current -0.03..1.29 A, 300 rows

steps.text: R = 1.982 ohm, L = 2.180 mH (tau 1.10 ms). Current PI by pole cancellation at 500 Hz, a twentieth of the 10 kHz loop rate to leave room for the one-sample delay: Kp = L*wc = 6.848 V/A, Ki = R*wc = 6225.9 V/(A s).

steps.name: set_current_pi
steps.summary: current loop Kp 6.848 V/A, Ki 6226 V/(A s)

steps.text: Now the mechanics: a constant current, and the acceleration it gives is Kt*i/J. I fit the slope only while the speed is low, so the back-EMF never limits the current, and I brake back to rest with the same current reversed.

steps.name: run
steps.summary: ran to 70.0 ms in current mode: speed 0 -> 88 rpm, current 1.25..1.55 A, 200 rows

steps.name: run
steps.summary: ran to 149.8 ms in current mode: speed 88 -> -88 rpm, current -1.60..0.44 A, 266 rows

steps.text: Acceleration 221 rad/s^2 at 1.44 A, so J/Kt = 6.514e-03 A s^2/rad. Speed PI at a tenth of the current loop (50 Hz): Kp = 0.2143 A/rpm, Ti = 12.7 ms, a 0.80 ms filter against encoder quantization, and anti-windup, since the start-up runs into the current limit.

steps.name: set_speed_pi
steps.summary: speed loop Kp 0.2143 A/rpm, Ki 16.83 A/(rpm s), anti-windup on, filter 0.796 ms

steps.name: run
steps.summary: ran to 169.8 ms in speed mode: speed -88 -> 0 rpm, current -1.83..7.23 A, 200 rows

steps.text: Check: the step to 3380 rpm, then the load on and off.
